description: Capability for thin detached windows (labels matching `detached-*`) — the single-surface Flavor-C windows from plans/multi-window. Loaded from the same localhost app URL as `main`. SCOPE OF THIS FILE: the Tauri ACL `permissions` array gates only PLUGIN + core commands, so withholding `sql:allow-execute`, `stronghold`, `dialog`, and `shell` here blocks the `@tauri-apps/plugin-*` JS paths for those plugins. The app's own `#[tauri::command]`s are granted in bulk via `allow-app-commands`, so a detached window has the same custom-command reach as `main` (secrets_*, db_exec, pty_*, supabase_config_*, fs_write, ...). That deliberately preserves pre-0.7.3 behaviour: before tauri 2.11.2 the ACL did not gate custom commands at all, so this window always had full reach. Since 2.11.2 it CAN be narrowed here — swapping `allow-app-commands` for a smaller per-window permission is now a real containment boundary, tracked as a follow-up. Until then, per-window restriction must still be enforced IN the command (inject `tauri::WebviewWindow` + reject non-privileged labels). The granted plugin perms are kept minimal (core IPC + event bus + read-only `sql:allow-select`/`allow-load`) as defense-in-depth. `core:window:allow-set-title` is granted on top of `core:window:default` (which covers reads only) so a detached surface can name its own OS window after its content — otherwise every pop-out is titled 'Ikenga' and they're indistinguishable in the window list. It only affects the calling window's own titlebar text.
